instructions: Put the 8 oz glass noodles in a large bowl and cover them with hot water from the kettle. Leave them to soak for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, slice the 8 oz sirloin against the grain into thin matchsticks about 1/4 inch thick. Toss them in a bowl with 1 tbsp of the soy sauce, 1 tsp of the sugar and 1 tbsp of the mirin.

In another bowl, stir together the rest of the soy sauce (1/4 cup), 1/2 cup water, the remaining 2 tbsp sugar, the remaining 2 tbsp mirin, 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil and the 1 tsp black pepper. Mince the 2 garlic cloves into it and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Thinly slice the onion and the red bell pepper. Peel the carrot and cut it into thin matchsticks. Cut the stems off the shiitake and slice the caps 1/4 inch thick.
Rinse the spinach well, shake off the water and cut off any thick stems.
Drain the noodles in a colander.

Heat 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over medium high. Add the onion, carrot and bell pepper with a pinch of salt and stir fry for 3 to 4 minutes, until they're soft but still have a little crunch.
Add the mushrooms and another pinch of salt and stir fry for 2 minutes, until they soften. Add the spinach and stir for about 1 minute, until it wilts. Transfer the vegetables onto a large plate.

Put the pan back over high heat with the last 1 tbsp vegetable oil. Spread the beef out in one layer and leave it for 1 minute so it browns. Stir fry it for 1 to 2 minutes, until no pink is left. Lift the beef onto the plate with the vegetables and leave the juices in the pan.

Turn the heat to medium. Add the noodles to the pan, pour the sauce over them and toss. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, tossing often, until the noodles are soft and chewy and have soaked up most of the liquid.
Turn the heat to low. Add the vegetables and beef back to the pan with the 1 tbsp sesame oil and the 1 tbsp sesame seeds. Toss until everything is mixed through the noodles.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
method_notes: All three read versions cook the vegetables and the beef separately and bring them together with the noodles and a soy, sugar, sesame oil and garlic sauce at the end. Beyond Kimchee soaks the noodles in hot water instead of boiling them and finishes them in the beef's pan juices with a watery sauce until it's absorbed. Korean Bapsang boils the noodles, blanches the spinach separately and tosses everything by hand in a bowl, and RecipeTin Eats marinates the beef briefly and tosses it all in a big bowl of sauce. This one follows Beyond Kimchee with a little more beef so it holds up as a dinner for 4.
